title: Height-Balanced Indexing for Idempotent Payment Webhook Processing in C#
topic: Your Payment Webhook Is Not a Notification. It s a Distributed Systems Problem.
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Payment webhooks are often treated as simple notifications, yet their idempotent processing in distributed environments imposes strict ordering and duplicate-suppression constraints. We present a height-balanced binary search tree that records webhook identifiers and timestamps, guaranteeing $O(\log N)$ insertion, deletion, and range queries while preserving a strict height-balance invariant. The tree is embedded in a C\# service that verifies signatures, enforces causal order via Lamport timestamps, and rejects duplicate events in constant time. Formal invariants are proven using a simple height-balance theorem, and static analysis confirms the absence of race conditions in the concurrent update path. Theoretical bounds are corroborated by an AST profile that shows a single function block and linear auxiliary memory. This work demonstrates that webhook handling can be modeled as a distributed state machine with provable safety properties. \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/csharp-enterprise-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261108_210232_your_payment_webhook_is_not_a}
